verification_report.summary:
The bounded repair is correct and resolves the sole critical error in common_barrier_compactness_01 without adding a mass bound. That historical report was read in full: its four named lemmas, capacity criterion, dominated corollary and actual applications remain accepted relative to their original local and separately audited inputs. The lower-barrier variant's previously passing mathematical proof is likewise retained. This audit checks only the replacement observation and the monotone-limit prerequisites throughout the section.

The corrected observation is already present at book/author/section_relative_compactness.tex:130. A decreasing sequence with a genuine limit has that limit as a fixed lower bound; a prescribed genuine lower barrier excludes collapse to identically -infinity. An increasing sequence has its genuine first term as a lower bound, and a common upper bound yields a genuine canonical upper semicontinuous limit. At fixed T, truncation gives bounded monotone capacity convergence. Outside the deep sublevel of the fixed genuine lower bound, the original functions equal their truncations. Taking the sequence limit first and then T to infinity proves capacity convergence by the accepted deep-sublevel capacity decay. No Monge-Ampere mass estimate enters.

Every monotone passage in the section has the required justification. The exponential-lemma truncations decrease to their given genuine potentials. The bounded upper tails A_j decrease to the given bounded a and have a constant lower barrier; alpha_j need not be monotone because it is sandwiched between a and A_j. The smooth decreasing regularizations target bounded genuine potentials and stay above them. In weighted lower semicontinuity, truncations target the given genuine potentials, while g_T are increasing scalar weights in [0,1]; positive-measure monotone convergence allows infinite mass. The scalar threshold limit introduces no potential-limit requirement.

For each fixed j, the finite rooftops p_{j,N} decrease above the admissible genuine competitor phi-C, so their limits p_j are genuine. The increasing p_j sequence has genuine first term p_1 and a common upper bound. The upper tails U_j decrease to the genuine canonical L1 limit u after the stipulated extraction and remain above phi-C. These statements hold both in the criterion and in its lower-barrier variant. In the variant, the upper bound C suffices: phi-C passes to u and prevents collapse. Its additional u preceq phi hypothesis retains its separate role in the accepted singularity-type and domination argument. The dominated corollary introduces no further monotone potential sequence; its deep-tail sets shrink to the pole set of genuine phi.

Thus the common-barrier prerequisites recorded conditionally in the passing bounded_subsolution_01 and weighted_measure_addition_01 reports are now available, relative to the same accepted inputs. The latter report's bounded-subsolution prerequisite is also supported by the existing passing bounded_subsolution_01 report. No new external result, uniform raw mass hypothesis, or uniform positive lower mass is introduced; the corollary's existing domination assumptions are unchanged. Sixteen statement checks and four reference/dependency records contain no errors or gaps. The book and all three prior reports were left unchanged, verified by SHA-256; the historical common_barrier_compactness_01 verdict remains wrong.
